**Titus** 1

*Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;*

*2 In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;*

*3 But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;*

*4 To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.*

*5 For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:*

*6 If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.*

*7 For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;*

*8 But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;*

*9 Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.*

*10 For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:*

*11 Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

*12 One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, the Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.*

*13 This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;*

*14 Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.*

*15 Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.*

*16 They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Paul, opens as he often does, professing he is a servant of God, and an Apostle, as evidenced by those who have believed his preaching unto salvation. His bona fides being those who believe. They having hope of eternal life, which God who cannot lie, promised before the world began, made manifest by the preaching of believers called to ministry of the Gospel. The preaching of this good news, which was commanded of Paul by Jesus Himself. The faith of those who received it of him bearing record. The fruit he has produced.

This comes up often in Acts, and in most of his letters, and it's important to understand why God chose to repeatedly make this point, that Paul was His Apostle, *born out of due time.*

There is heresy out there calling in to question Paul's authority, and casting doubt on his writings and doctrines, which make up a bulk of the NT books. Doubt that wicked men seek to cast to keep those ignorant of the truth from ever considering the epistles as scripture, not understanding that there is a perfect consistency between the inspired words of the prophets, patriarchs, Christ Jesus and His Apostles. Let alone considering the need of the clarity of doctrine regarding the implications of the common faith, of eternal life, by Grace. The mystery being revealed by the manifestation of Jesus in the flesh, His death, burial and His resurrection. Of how we are to partake in the promise, and having been adopted by God into His Kingdom, what then? What's next, having been saved?

And so, thank God, He sought to give us the epistles, that we may be more perfect in our understanding. Just as He gave us the prophets, that we could be made meet for repentance, and the Gospels so we may know what we are to turn towards, we are given the Acts and letters of the apostles so we may know what we should do once we have turned toward God. And Revelation of Jesus Christ, that we may know what is to come.

It is all one word, one testimony, one book made up of 66 smaller books, written over thousands of years, but with one voice, the inspiration of God, through the Spirit, testifying of the Son.

Sometimes people lose sight of this. People who having believed the word, and should know better, as they have the same Spirit testifying to its power, within them.

It is never so important to keep this in mind as when reading the Pastoral Epistles, 1st and 2nd Timothy, which we covered this past few weeks, and Titus today.

At issue is the original organization of local churches. Of the offices and expectations, and the doctrines that should be preserved and taught among the congregations.

Even supposed Christian denominations, especially those that claim an "Apostolic Tradition," will cast doubt on the epistles, denying Paul's authority by countermanding his doctrines, ignoring them, or claiming there were oral tradition that differs significantly from the whole body of scripture that contradicts their own edicts.

There's a saying in studying scripture, that nothing in God's word is coincidental, incidental or accidental. And a maxim that if God repeats something, it is for emphasis and our edification. That it's important for us to get it. Much of scripture is terse, and brief and pithy. Giving exactly enough to convey the message intended. So, when God repeats the same lesson, we should listen.

The Pastoral Epistles are an excellent example of this. One cannot say "Well, Paul was just telling Timothy this, we can't claim it's in all cases..." when he repeats the same doctrines to Titus. Just as Jude and Peter wrote nearly identical messages to the churches, just as we have four Gospel accounts. God's perfect judgement calls for multiple witness to establish truth, and He provides the same for us that we may believe Him, and those He sent.

This epistle, written to Titus, Paul's son in the faith, who the Apostle had left in Crete to evangelize, just as he had Timothy in Ephesus.

And just as he did in his letters to Timothy, Paul lays the foundation for the office of bishop, or pastor in today's parlance, a shepherd of the flock, and deacons or elders, those who work in a church ministering, serving the flock and aiding their shepherd.

 Commanding Titus to *ordain elders in every city,* the criteria being; *blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.* Because, as the steward of God, the man handling the affairs and overseeing His sheep, must have these qualities; *not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate.*

Not given to wine and sober not being repetitive notions, but sober in scripture meaning not only clear-headed but serious as well. Matured in their attitudes. Not angry and wrathful and violent. Not a lover of money, corrupt, chasing after filthy lucre. A lover of hospitality and good men. *Just, holy and temperate*.

This is the model for all seeking the offices of pastor or deacon, and should be what is given as an example for all young men of the faith to strive towards. Not only those who "feel a calling," but those who in humility and meekness seek to be right with God, that they may be blameless and able to win souls to the Lord.

*Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.*

This should be the goal of all those who know Christ. Studying to be approved by God, and able to have a ready answer to those who seek truth, or who having hardened their hearts, seek to subvert it.

And why is this so important to establish, especially with elders in the churches? Paul tells us, again warning as he has repeatedly, of those reprobate concerning the faith.

*For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

Even in Paul's day, even in that first century, not far removed from Jesus'resurrection and ascension, even as Apostles and disciples blessed with the gifts of the Holy Ghost spread the word, preaching to every creature throughout the world, there were *many* false prophets. Vain talkers. Especially of the circumcision. Jews who being reprobate by God sought to subvert the nascent Christian communities with deceit, just as they do today.

Paul gives an example of one such viper, who insulting the Cretians sought to keep them from the faith, and exhorts Titus to openly rebuke. To teach sound doctrines that the Cretian believers not be led astray, *giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.*

Judaizers who attacked the word of God and His churches then, never gave up, even forming their own religions based on Jewish fables, the apocryphal books and forgeries prevalent at the time. Doing it for filthy lucre's sake. For money, power, prestige. Control of others. Leaning on their own understanding, denying the power of scripture. Following after vain traditions and the commandments of men. Dead works, denying the power of the Gospel and faith unto salvation.

This is the origin of the Roman Catholic Church, and the source of her harlot daughters, subverting whole houses. Who *compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than* themselves, as Jesus said of the same Judaizers who murdered Him.

Who could do such things? What kind of man could be so contrary to all other men, that they'd seek to subvert and damn others, as they are? Just as their father, the devil seeks to? Reprobates. Conscience seared, defiled, twice-dead. Deserving death.

*Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Every ordained Catholic priest, cardinal and 'pope.' Every Orthodox monk and Anglican bishop. Every works-based false salvationist. Every cult leader of LDS or JW. Calvinist lordshiper 'reformed' viper, with their corrupt modern translations. All of them.

They are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness. And over and over again scripture teaches us to be Biblical Fundamentalists, to cling to God's word, and to reject those who seek to turn others from the truth. Others who, with itching ears and mired in their own sins, can be turned from the truth by these vain talkers. Their mouths must be stopped, and it is by the word of God that we shut them up.

**Titus 1**

*1 Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;*

*2 In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;*

*3 But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;*

*4 To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.*

*5 For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:*

*6 If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.*

*7 For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;*

*8 But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;*

*9 Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.*

*10 For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:*

*11 Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

*12 One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, the Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.*

*13 This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;*

*14 Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.*

*15 Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.*

*16 They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the *elect*, or chosen.

When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected:

"*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them."* **Jeremiah 6:30**

This deliberate use is misinterpreted by calvanists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness.

To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return.

This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

**Titus 2**

*But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:*

*2 That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.*

*3 The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;*

*4 That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,*

*5 To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.*

*6 Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.*

*7 In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,*

*8 Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.*

*9 Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again;*

*10 Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.*

*11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,*

*12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;*

*13 Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;*

*14 Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.*

*15 These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.*

Chapter 2 is a direct continuation of the same thought in chapter 1 (reminder that these divisions we're not in scripture and often seem clunky and forced). The "But" sets in contrast the reprobates being talked about at the end of chapter 1, to provide counterpoint to what Titus should teach and preach instead. Sound doctrines.

That Christian men be sober and grave, clear minded and serious. Temperate, not given to wrath or over emotional, but instead being calm and measured. Sound in faith, trusting God, and in charity and patience, reflecting the love, mercy, longsuffering and grace God gave them, on to others.

That women do likewise, behaving in holiness, not false accusers, drunken, but teachers of good things. Women being the teachers at home of the children, especially young women, so they may know how they ought to behave and that the young men learn to be sober minded as well. And that they all are given to doing good works out of the abundance of their heart, because of the sound doctrine they have been taught.

This is all to serve the glory of God, to make us blameless that we may share His Gospel. That the word of God be not blasphemed.

We are at Liberty in Christ. We aren't going to be judged by our works for justification before God, but we are judged of man. We are to be good witnesses to others, for the unbelieving's sake. That they may be called by the light of truth we magnify. To become the vessels of gold and silver, meet for the master's use. To be more perfect in our faith. To earn glory in the Kingdom which we are joint heirs.

The Bible says everything else is vanity.

But the occasion to blaspheme God by being a bad witness should also motivate us. That the devil is an accuser of the brethren. A ravenous lion seeking whom he may devour. By our sin as believers, we give him cause to blaspheme God.

When Nathan reproaches David in his sin with Uriah the Hittite and Bathsheba, he says that David's sins of murder and adultery are already forgiven, as David was saved by faith. But *because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme,* God punishes David with the death of his newborn son.

We too face reproach and punishment by God for being a bad witness to His power. He scourges His children for giving His enemies reason to blaspheme. For bringing dishonor to His house.

*In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.*

This ties in with the much-abused James 2, and the exhortation of believers to do good works, that their faith be profitable to others, knowing that a man may judge their faith by their works.

And again it's in furtherance of spreading the Gospel.

We obey the commandments out of love and do good works out of love, that we being honor to the house of our Lord, and build His congregation with new believers. Edifying the church. This is our calling. All else is vanity.

Paul continues, again as he has in other epistles, instructing that servants, indentured or employed, be honest and diligent. That they may show through their behavior the glory of the grace of God, who is not a respecter of persons.

*God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.* The lowly and the high status are all judged the same. *When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom. Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.*

This is a difficult saying, but it is found all through scripture. We are to be satisfied with our station, and be joyous in our salvation.

*Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.*

Knowing this, and knowing it is God's grace that sets us free, we shouldn't resent our station, and instead be thankful for what we have, blameless that we may win even those who we serve to Christ.

And so, living uprightly and blamelessly, having *Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you,* we humble ourselves, *esteeming others better than ourselves.*

*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.*

And again, as Jesus taught us;

*And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.*

*Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

*For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same? And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?*

*Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.*

The faith required to give up pride, knowing that God will reward you in the next life for wrongs suffered in this one, is one of the hardest hurdles we face in our Christian walk.

And for what cause do we humble ourselves, living soberly and with all gravity? Giving good witness? Blameless that we may not be accused? Rendering good works and a meek answer for our hope, given with a clear conscience?

*For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.*

*These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority.*

*Let no man despise thee.*

We who are saved by faith, who have that blessed hope, an assurance given us by the Spirit, testifying within us. The new man, quickened, warning against the flesh, we have the grace of God teaching us that these things are so, and good, and right, and so me must exhort other believers to this cause, and rebuke those who oppose it, with all authority as His peculiar people. His preisthood of believers. To His glory, forever and ever.

Amen

**Titus 3**

*Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work,*

*2 To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.*

*3 For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.*

*4 But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,*

*5 Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;*

*6 Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;*

*7 That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

*8 This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.*

*9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.*

*10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;*

*11 Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.*

*12 When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.*

*13 Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.*

*14 And let our's also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.*

*15 All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.*

Finishing Titus, Paul continues his exhortation to teach sound and profitable doctrine to the Cretians. Letting no man despise Titus for the truth, encouraging him and those who he sets up as pastors and elders in the churches he plants as evangelist to make certain they have the the same doctrines of faith.

This instruction has given us as men, women, girls and boys, servants and slaves, leaders and pastors the blueprint for Christian living. Continuing the theme, Paul writes, again, that we must subject ourselves to higher powers, even as we keep God as the highest. *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men,* as he writes in Romans.

And again, this is to make us blameless that we may win people who are in error, bringing them to repentance towards God and common salvation. Being a good witness. This is a hard saying, and pride, fear and wrath lead many to stumble at it.

We are warned to speak evil of no man, because after all, the sins and flaws that they may be engaged in are sins common to man, and such were we at times. But with the kindness and mercy God showed us, so too we are to extend grace towards others that they may be drawn to the light. As Jesus taught, *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

And this is the purpose of good works, to be profitable to other men in showing them the light of God. Not to justify us before God, but that others may step into the light by our example. That works are not how we are saved is the clearest, most repeated doctrine in scripture, and yet it continues to be the stumbling block that keeps so many perishing, damned to Hell because they trust in their self righteousness to save them.

It couldn't be any clearer than in Titus 3:

...*That the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

There is no doubt we are saved from our sins and Hell by faith alone, by grace alone, in Christ alone. That God's grace extends to all men. That the renewing of our spirit comes from the Holy Ghost, and He through our faith in Jesus Christ, and God's promise that we be His heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven in the assurance of eternal life.

This is the Gospel. There is nothing more to it. There can be nothing less.

And to put works firmly in the place where they belong, to be encouraged in the life of those who are already saved, that we may be in service to those who have yet to be. (And no, they aren't automatic, as some false prophets preach, for if they were then we wouldn't need so much encouragement to commit ourselves to them)

*This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.*

This is the Biblical Doctrine of good works. That they which *have believed*, past tense, in the Gospel that was just laid out, *might* do them and be profitable to others.

We are justified by His grace. And so we should be reminded of that and do good works that others may benefit from our salvation.

If your theology is anything else, repent. You're perishing. As wise and as knowledgeable to the doctrines of man as you might be, don't let your pride mislead you from the clear truth presented here, and throughout scripture.

And, once again, God repeats for emphasis that we should avoid foolish questions, Jewish fables, endless genealogies, and strivings about the law; *for they are unprofitable and vain*.

Debates and silly theological questions and talmudic arguments about the law help no one. They can lead to heresy and blasphemy. They can be a snare and a stumbling block to those seeking truth. Be determined to know nothing but Christ and Him crucified.

As far as those who endlessly strive about these things? They are heretics.

*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*

If you've shown them clear scripture, two times, and they still insist they are right, then shake the dust. It's not worth it to answer a fool in his folly. It's why I have the pinned rules in my chat. Sincerely asked questions, met with polite consideration when answered is one thing, but demands to go back and forth with their natural man idea of scripture is vanity. Useless. Helping no one, and may give you cause to sin and them to accuse.

*Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself* be satisfied, instead of having to prove them wrong. That's your pride, and it helps no one. (I have fallen in to this trap. It's so tempting)

Grace be with you all. Amen.

For those keeping track at home, together we have read every book in the New Testament except for Mark and Luke, 1st and 2nd Peter, revelation and Philemon.(although we've done studies out of all of them).

And in all of these verse by verse breakdowns, we have yet to find any hint of salvation with works, lordship, calvinism, sacraments, man-made Church denominations, the authority of man to add to the word, or any other popular heresy.

Clear verses, in context, and all of these doctrines remain unmentioned, while the clear teaching of salvation by faith alone through grace alone in Christ alone is given. Over and over again. Really makes you think...

A common argument made by heretics who haven't taken correction after one or two admonishments with scripture is that "only God can judge if I am wrong."

And while that's true, we are blessed to know His judgment as God has laid out precisely what the correct doctrine of salvation is in a way that's clear and understandable.

Don't assume one's relationship with God by their works or sins. It's hypocritical and you don't know the full story, nor can you know where the Spirit may lead them.

But you can absolutely judge by their doctrine. And if they tell you they don't believe the Gospel and are trusting in something other than it to be justified, you can safely consider them unsaved.

What makes all these staged acts of vandalism doubly galling is that they involve wasting food at a time of growing fears of famine and inflation.

Our instinct at times like this is to be shocked at deliberately wasting food. It's why they aren't using paint or anything else.
